title: Don't Be a Bunch of Fanboys
paragraphs: §Divisions in the Church

What's up, guys? It's Paul, and I'm writing this with my buddy Sosthenes. Jesus himself, the Messiah, hand-picked me for this gig. This letter is for the church crew in Corinth, all of you who've been given a fresh start by Jesus and are on this awesome journey with God. And a shout-out to everyone, everywhere, who's on Team Jesus. He's their Master as well as ours!
Hope you guys get all the awesome perks and blessings from God our Father and our main man, Jesus.

I'm not gonna lie, I think about you guys a lot, and every time I do, I'm so stoked for you. You've got a direct line to God because of Jesus, and the transformation in your lives is for real. It's not just talk; you're living proof that Christ is the real deal.

Seriously, you guys are set. You have everything you need. All of God's gifts are yours for the taking while you wait for the epic return of Jesus. And get this: God's got your back the whole time, making sure you don't get off track. He's the one who got you into this whole thing, and He's not going to ghost you. He's in it for the long haul.

Alright, real talk, guys. I've gotta get serious for a minute, and I'm saying this with all the authority Jesus gave me. You've gotta stop fighting. Seriously. I heard from Chloe's family that you're all picking teams, like you're in some kind of fantasy league. "I'm with Paul!" "Nah, Apollos is my guy!" "Peter's the real MVP!" "I'm only on Team Messiah!" Are you kidding me? Did Jesus get chopped up into little pieces for you to claim? Was I the one who got crucified for you? Did any of you get baptized in my name? I'm actually glad I didn't baptize most of you, except for Crispus and Gaius, so nobody can claim I was building my own little fan club. Oh yeah, and I baptized Stephanas's family, but that's it.

Look, God didn't send me to get a bunch of followers for myself. He sent me to tell everyone the good news about Jesus, and not with a bunch of fancy words that would make the cross seem like no big deal. The story of the cross sounds like total nonsense to people who are headed for destruction, but for us who are being saved, it's where the real power is at. God even said, "I'm gonna make all the 'smart' people look clueless and expose the so-called experts."

So where are all the geniuses and philosophers now? God made all their 'wisdom' look like a joke. The world, with all its smarts, couldn't figure God out. So God, in his genius, decided to use what the world thinks is a foolish message—preaching about Jesus—to save everyone who trusts in him.

Some people want to see big, flashy miracles, and others want to hear some deep, philosophical arguments. But we're just gonna keep telling everyone about Christ, the one who was crucified. To some, that's a total deal-breaker, and to others, it's just plain ridiculous. But to us, the ones God has called, Christ is the ultimate power and wisdom of God. What looks like God's weakness is way stronger than any human strength, and what looks like God's foolishness is way smarter than any human wisdom.

Think about it, guys. When God called you, not many of you were the popular kids, the influencers, or the ones from rich families. God totally did that on purpose. He chose the nobodies to show the somebodies that they're not all that. That way, nobody can brag about how great they are in front of God. Everything we have—being right with God, living right, a clean slate, a fresh start—it all comes from God through Jesus. So if you're gonna brag, brag about how awesome God is.

title: God's Secret Plan
paragraphs: §God's Wisdom vs. World's Wisdom

Remember when I first showed up to tell you about God's master plan? I didn't come at you with some slick TED Talk or crazy new ideas. Nah, I kept it real simple: It's all about Jesus, who he is, and the realest thing he ever did – dying on the cross.

Honestly, I was kinda panicking. I felt like a total noob and was super nervous. So, nothing I said was all that impressive. But the message still hit home, right? That was all God. His Spirit showed his power, proving that your faith isn't about me being some smooth talker, but about God's raw power.

Once you're solid in your faith, we've got some next-level wisdom to share. This isn't the kind of stuff you hear from so-called experts that's trending one day and cringe the next. God's wisdom is like a secret level in a video game; it's deep and has been around forever. It's God's ultimate strategy to help us have a miraculous transformation. The so-called 'experts' of our time? They were clueless. If they had any idea, they wouldn't have killed the Master of the God-designed life. It's like the old-school verse says: 'No one has ever seen, heard, or even imagined the awesome stuff God has lined up for those who are on his team.' But you guys? You get the inside scoop because God's Spirit reveals it all.

The Spirit isn't just scratching the surface; it's diving deep into God's plans and showing us what's up. Think about it: who knows what you're thinking better than you? Same with God. But the cool part is, He lets us in on His thoughts. He gives us the full rundown on the awesome gifts of life and salvation. We don't need to guess or listen to what the world thinks. We didn't learn this from a book or in a classroom; God taught us directly through Jesus, and now we're passing it on to you, no filter.

Someone who's not on a spiritual level just can't get what God's Spirit is offering. It all sounds like nonsense to them. You can only understand spiritual things with the Spirit. When you're spiritually alive, you have an all-access pass to what God is doing, and you can't be judged by the haters. Remember that old question, 'Who can possibly know what God is thinking or doing?' Well, we've got the answer: Christ knows, and we have his Spirit. So we're in on the secret.

title: Quit Acting Like Babies
paragraphs: §Spiritual Maturity

I'm getting frustrated with you guys, for real. You're not acting right with each other or with God. You're like a bunch of babies when it comes to Jesus, just wanting to be spoon-fed. Fine, I'll treat you like babies since you're acting like it. As long as you're just doing whatever feels good and makes you look cool, you're no different than a little kid who only wants his way. When one of you is like, "I'm on Team Paul," and another is like, "I'm with Apollos," aren't you just being totally childish?

Like, who do you even think we are? Paul? Apollos? We're just the guys who helped you get to know the real Boss. We each had our own job to do. I planted the seed, Apollos watered it, but God was the one who made it grow. So it's not about who planted or who watered, it's all about God, who makes things happen. Planting and watering are just the grunt work. The real reward is serving God. You guys are like God's garden that we're working in.

Or think of it like this: you're God's house. God gave me the skills to be a good architect, so I drew up the plans. Apollos is building the walls. But every builder who comes along needs to be careful how they build. There's only one foundation, and that's Jesus Christ. You gotta be careful what you build with. Sooner or later, there's gonna be a vibe check. If you use cheap, weak stuff, you'll be exposed. The inspection is gonna be intense, and you won't get away with anything. If your work is solid, you're good. If not, your part of the building gets torn down and you have to start over. But you'll be safe, but just barely, like you escaped a fire.

You get that you're God's temple, right? And that God is literally living in you? Nobody gets away with messing up God's temple, you can bet on that. God's temple is a sacred space, and that's you, so don't forget it.

Don't play yourself. Don't think you're smart just because you're trendy. Be a fool for God—that's how you get real wisdom. What the world thinks is smart, God calls clueless. It's in the book: He roasts the fakes and sees right through the know-it-alls.

So I don't want to hear any of you flexing about yourselves or anyone else. Everything is already yours. Paul, Apollos, Peter, the world, life, death, now, the future—it's all yours. And you're privileged to be in union with Christ, who's tight with God.

title: Who Do You Think You Are?
paragraphs: §Servants of Christ

Alright, so here's the deal. Don't get it twisted and think we're some big-shot masters. We're just servants of Christ, like his roadies, setting up the stage for his big show. We're the ones who hold the keys to God's secret playbook, not some high-and-mighty security guards. And what's the number one rule for a roadie? Be reliable and know your stuff. Honestly, I couldn't care less what you guys think of me, or where I rank on your popularity contest. I don't even rank myself. It's pointless. I know I'm not perfect, but that's not for me to decide. The only one who gets to judge me is the big boss, God himself.

So, chill with the judging, you guys. Don't jump to conclusions before all the evidence is in. When Jesus comes back, he's gonna put everything out in the open. All the secret thoughts, the hidden motives, everything. That's when we'll find out who gets the real “well done” from God.

I'm using myself and Apollos as an example so you can learn to cool it with the comparisons. Stop gassing up one guy and dissing another based on rumors. It's all about what God thinks, not what you hear through the grapevine.

Seriously, who do you think you are? Who knows what's really in your heart? And even if they did, what do you have that you didn't get as a gift from God? Everything you have, everything you are, is a total gift. So why are you all puffed up and acting like you earned it all yourselves? You guys think you're all that, sitting on top of the world. But we're right there with you, even if you don't see it.

It feels like God put us apostles on display in a stadium where nobody wants to buy a ticket. We're like a car crash that everyone gawks at. We're the Messiah's misfits. You guys are so sure of yourselves, while we're just a bunch of weak and insecure guys. You're popular and well-liked, and we get kicked around like stray dogs. We're hungry, our clothes are ripped, and we get doors slammed in our faces. We work odd jobs just to get by. When people roast us, we bless them. When they spread lies about us, we say something nice about them. We're treated like dirt, the leftovers nobody wants. And it's not getting any better.

I'm not telling you all this to make you feel bad. I'm writing to you like a dad, like my own kids. I love you and I want you to grow up right, not spoiled. There are plenty of people who will tell you what you're doing wrong, but not many who will stick around and help you grow up. I became your spiritual dad when I shared the message of Jesus with you. And I'm not asking you to do anything I'm not doing myself.
That's why I sent my boy Timothy to you. He's my right-hand man, and he's solid with the Lord. He'll remind you of the way I live and the things I teach in all the churches.

I know some of you are so full of yourselves that you don't listen to anyone, especially not me. You think I'm never gonna show up in person. But I'll be there sooner than you think, God willing. And then we'll see if you're all talk or if you've got some real power from God. Because God's kingdom isn't about a bunch of hot air; it's about a life with real power.
So, what's it gonna be? You want me to come as a drill sergeant and whip you into shape? Or as a good friend who wants to have a heart-to-heart? You decide.

title: Time to Clean House
paragraphs: §Dealing with Sin in the Church

Hey, I can't even believe the gossip I'm hearing about your church. There's some seriously messed-up stuff going on, the kind of drama that even people outside the church would call out. One of your own guys is having an affair with his stepmom! And what’s crazier is that you guys are acting all high and mighty, like it doesn't even bother you. Seriously? Shouldn't this totally wreck you? Shouldn't you be heartbroken? This guy and his toxic behavior need to be called out and dealt with, like, yesterday.

Listen up, here's the play. Even though I'm not there with you, just imagine I am, because I see exactly what's happening. This is so not okay. You can't just ghost this problem and hope it disappears. You have to put it on blast and handle it with the power of our leader, Jesus. Get the whole crew together—I'll be there in spirit, and you know Jesus will be there flexing His power. Put this guy on the spot in front of everyone. Let him try to defend himself. If he can't, he's gotta go. Yeah, it's gonna be a total gut-punch for him and super awkward for you, but it's way better than him getting totally wrecked on Judgment Day. The goal is to get him to wake up and get right with God before it's too late.

Honestly, your cocky attitude about all this is what's really getting to me. You're acting like it's no big deal, but it's a huge deal. Think about it: it only takes a tiny bit of yeast to make a whole batch of bread dough puff up. It's the same with this kind of bad vibe—it spreads like wildfire and infects the whole crew. So, you need to get rid of that toxic yeast before it ruins everything. Here's the real you: plain and true, not puffed up with garbage. The Messiah, our Passover Lamb, already gave everything for us, so let's keep it honest—no shady stuff, just truth. Now, I'm not saying you should ghost everyone outside the church who lives messy. You'd have to leave the planet for that. But when someone who calls themselves a Christian keeps living in sin—sleeping around, scamming people, dissing God, getting wasted, being greedy—don't just act like it's all good. Judging people outside the church isn't your job; God handles them. But inside the crew? Yeah, you need to deal with it. If someone's way out of line, clean house.

title: Don't Be a Court-Tattler
paragraphs: §Lawsuits and Your Body

Seriously, you guys have beef with each other and you're gonna drag them to court? In front of judges who don't even know God? That's a major facepalm. You do realize that one day, we're gonna be the ones judging the whole world, right? So if you're gonna be ruling on huge stuff like that, can't you handle these little squabbles in your own squad? We're even going to be judging angels, my guy! So why are you taking your everyday drama to people you wouldn't trust with anything else?

I'm being super blunt to show you how lame this is. Is there really not one single person in your whole group who can be a fair ref when you guys have issues? I don't buy it. But here you are, suing each other in front of people who don't even roll with God. How are they supposed to give you real justice if they don't even believe in the God who invented it?

Honestly, these lawsuits are giving your crew a bad rep. Wouldn't it be better to just take the L, let it go, and move on? Instead, you're just making things worse, hurting your own spiritual family. That's not how we do things.

Don't you get it? People who are all about themselves and don't care about God won't be joining his kingdom. The people who just use and abuse others, who are messed up with sex, and trash the planet—they're not on the guest list for God's kingdom. Some of you used to be on that list, so you know what I'm talking about. But you got a miraculous transformation. You've been cleaned up and given a fresh start by Jesus, our boss, and by God's Spirit living in us.

Just because something is technically allowed doesn't mean it's good for you. If I just did whatever I wanted all the time, I'd basically be a slave to my own moods. That's not freedom, that's a trap.

You know that saying, "Food for the stomach and the stomach for food"? Yeah, well, your body isn't just a temporary container for whatever you want to stuff in it, whether it's too much pizza or random hookups. The Boss honors you with a body, so you should honor him with yours.

God flexed his power by raising Jesus from the dead, and he's gonna do the same for you. Until then, remember your body is just as important as the Boss's. You wouldn't take Jesus' body to a suspicious place, would you? I hope not.

And look, sex is a way bigger deal than just skin-on-skin. It's a spiritual thing. The old book says, "the two become one." Since we're trying to be one with the Boss, we can't be chasing after the kind of sex that's all about the moment and leaves you feeling empty and alone. That's not real connection. Messing up with sex is different from other sins because you're disrespecting your own body, which is supposed to be a sacred space, like God's crib. Didn't you know the Holy Spirit lives in you? You can't just live however you want, throwing away this amazing gift God paid a huge price for. Your body isn't just your property to do whatever with. God owns the whole you. So let people see God's awesomeness in how you live and how you treat your body.

title: Single, Married, or It's Complicated?
paragraphs: §On Marriage and Singleness

Alright, let's get into the stuff you guys asked about. First up: the whole deal with relationships. Is it better to just stay single? Honestly, yeah, being single is a good way to go, but let's be real, hormones are a thing. So, getting married is a solid way to handle all that in a good way, instead of getting into all the drama out there. Marriage is a team sport. It's not about what you can get, it's about making your partner happy. It's a total partnership, inside the bedroom and out. You can't just be all about your own needs. If you both decide to take a break from being intimate, that's cool, but it has to be a mutual decision, and for a good reason, like focusing on your faith. But don't stay apart for too long, because that's when things can get messy and you might get tempted. I'm not making this a rule, just giving you some solid advice.

Sometimes I think it would be easier if everyone was single like me. Life is way less complicated! But being single isn't for everyone, just like marriage isn't for everyone. God has a different plan for each of us; for some it's the single life, for others it's marriage.

For all the single people and widows out there, I'm telling you, being single can be awesome. It works for me. But if you're struggling with being single and can't stop thinking about relationships, then you should totally get married. It's way better to deal with the challenges of marriage than to be miserable and single.

If you're married, stay married. That's a direct order from the big guy, not just my opinion. If a wife leaves her husband, she either needs to stay single or go back and work things out. And a husband can't just ditch his wife.

Now, for those of you in a relationship with someone who isn't a believer, there's no direct rule from God on this. So here's my take: if you're a guy and your wife isn't a believer but she wants to stay with you, then stay with her. Same for the ladies, if your husband isn't a believer but he wants to make it work, then stick with him. The non-believing partner gets some of the spiritual perks from the believing one, and your kids are included in God's plan too.

But, if the non-believing partner decides to bounce, you have to let them go. Don't force it. God wants us to live in peace. And who knows? Maybe the way you handle the situation will make your partner come back to you and even find their own faith.

Don't waste your time wishing you were somewhere else or with someone else. God has you right where you need to be. So live your life, be faithful, and love God right where you are. Your relationship status doesn't define you, God does. And I'm not just saying this to you guys, I tell this to all the churches.
Were you Jewish when God called you? Don't try to hide it. Were you not Jewish? Don't feel like you have to become one. None of that matters. What's important is that you follow God's plan for you.

Whatever you were doing when God called you, just keep doing it. Were you a slave? That doesn't stop you from being a believer. If you get a chance to be free, take it. But being a follower of Christ gives you a whole new kind of freedom you've never experienced before. And if you were free when you were called, you'll find a new purpose in serving God.
You were all bought with a price, so don't go back to living the way everyone else does. Stay true to what God has called you to be. He's right there with you.

Now, about the virgins. The Master didn't give any specific instructions, but I've been through a lot and I'm loyal to him, so you can trust my advice. With all the craziness going on in the world, it's probably best to just stay as you are. If you're married, stay married. If you're single, don't rush into marriage. But it's not a sin to get married. I'm just saying that marriage adds a whole new level of stress to your life, and I want to save you from that if I can.
Time is short, my friends. So don't make your lives more complicated than they need to be. Keep it simple, no matter what you're going through. This world isn't going to last forever.

I want you to live a life with as few distractions as possible. When you're single, you can focus all your energy on pleasing God. When you're married, you have to think about your spouse's needs too, which can pull your attention in a million different directions. The time and energy that married people spend on each other, single people can use to become better servants of God. I'm not trying to make things harder for you, I'm trying to help you live a life where you can be close to God without a lot of drama.

If a guy has a female friend that he's close to but never planned on marrying, and then he changes his mind, he should go for it. It's not a sin. But if he's happy with his decision to be single and serve God, he should stick with it. Marriage is a good thing, but in these crazy times, I think being single is a better way to go.

A wife should stay with her husband for as long as he lives. If he dies, she's free to marry whoever she wants, as long as he's a believer. But in my opinion, she'd be better off staying single. And I think God agrees with me.

title: To Eat or Not to Eat the Idol Meat
paragraphs: §Food Offered to Idols

Alright, so everyone's been blowing up my messages about this whole thing with eating meat that was part of some idol worship. Like, can you go to a party where they're serving that stuff or not? A lot of you guys think you're so smart and have it all figured out. But honestly, being a know-it-all just puffs up your ego. It's love that really builds people up. If you think you're a genius, you're probably missing the point. The real transformation happens when you realize God's the one who knows everything, and what really matters is that you love Him.

Look, we all know those idols are just statues, basically lawn ornaments. They're not real. Everyone knows there's only one true God, the Father. He's the one who made everything, and we're living for him. And there's one Master, our main man Jesus, and everything is for his sake, including us. That's a fact. Seriously.

But here's the deal: not everyone in the squad is on the same level. Some of the newer guys are still sketched out by this stuff. They've spent their whole lives thinking that idol meat is seriously bad news, and eating it messes you up inside. You can't expect them to just get over that overnight. So even though you know the meat is fine, you gotta be sensitive to the fact that they're not there yet.

God isn't going to grade you based on what you eat. You don't get extra points for eating the suspicious meat, and you don't get a penalty for skipping it. But He *does* care if you flex your freedom in a way that trips up one of your friends who's still struggling with it. That's a major party foul.

Think about it. Let's say you, Mr. Know-It-All, go to some pagan BBQ at an idol's temple and start chowing down. What happens if a newer Christian, who looks up to you, sees you do that? He's going to get super confused. He might even think, "Well, if he's doing it, I guess it's okay," and then do something his own heart tells him is wrong. You just peer-pressured him into messing up.

Christ died for that person. Are you seriously telling me you can't give up a burger for him? When you hurt your friend like that, you're actually hurting Christ. It's not worth it. So if there's even a tiny chance that eating that food will cause one of your brothers or sisters to stumble, just don't do it. I'd rather go vegan for life than mess up one of my friends.

title: Why I Don't Get Paid for This Gig
paragraphs: §Paul's Rights as an Apostle

Hey, don't even start with the "you're not the boss of me" talk. I'm totally free to do what I'm doing, isn't it obvious? I've got a mission, a face-to-face commission from Jesus himself. You guys are living proof that I'm legit. Even if everyone else ghosts me, you can't. My work with you is the ultimate receipt.

And for the haters, I'm not afraid to clap back. We're on God's missionary team, so we've earned the right to a decent place to crash and for our families to be taken care of. You don't see anyone questioning the other apostles or Jesus's own brothers, or even Peter. So why me? Is it just me and Barnabas who have to hustle on our own? Soldiers don't pay for their own gear, right? Gardeners get to eat their own veggies. And you know the farmer gets to drink the milk.

I'm not just popping off because I'm salty. This is ancient wisdom. Moses said, "Don't muzzle the ox when it's working." You think he was only worried about cows? Nah, he was talking about us too. When you plant seeds, you expect to eat, right? So if we've planted all this spiritual stuff in you, is it too much to ask for a meal? Other people are getting plenty from you. Don't we deserve even more, since we've never asked for anything?

But look, we're not about to start demanding stuff now. We've always chosen to just deal with it rather than get in the way of the message about Christ. I just don't want you to use our chill to take advantage of other people. You know how it works: the guys who work in the Temple get to eat from the Temple's stash. The ones who do the sacrifices get a cut. Jesus said the same thing: those who spread the good news should be supported by the people who hear it.

But I've never taken a dime, and I'm not writing this to get paid now. I'd rather die than have someone say I'm just in it for the money. Preaching the message isn't about me getting a paycheck. I *have* to do it. It's my calling. If this was just some side work I came up with, I'd expect to get paid. But it's a sacred trust. So what's my reward? The awesome feeling of sharing this message with you for free. You don't even have to cover my travel expenses!

Even though I'm a free agent, I've basically become everyone's servant to try and reach all kinds of people. I'm talking church kids, non-church kids, the super-strict rule-followers, the wild ones, the ones who feel like they've lost, and the totally burned out. I don't live like them, I stay true to Christ, but I get in their world to see where they're coming from. I've become whatever I need to be to help people get saved. I do it all for the message. I don't just want to talk about it; I want to be a part of it.

You've all seen a track meet. Everyone runs, but only one person gets the trophy. So run to win! Every serious athlete trains like crazy. They do it for a medal that's just going to get old and dusty. But you're going for the eternal gold.

So I'm not jogging, I'm sprinting for the finish line. I'm all in. No lazy days for me. I'm staying sharp and in the zone. I'm not about to tell everyone else how to win and then get disqualified myself.

title: Don't Get Cocky
paragraphs: §Warnings from History

Hey, listen up. We gotta remember our history so we don't mess up like our ancestors did. They were all led by a massive cloud and walked right through the sea like it was nothing. They got baptized, basically, with Moses leading them from being slaves to being free. They all ate the same magic food and drank from the same magic rock that followed them around, which was actually Christ. But even with all that, most of them blew it and got taken out in the desert because they couldn't handle the tough times. God was not happy.

That same stuff can happen to us. We gotta be careful not to get all selfish and demand our own way. And we can't turn our faith into a wild party like they did. They partied, and then things got way out of hand. We can't be messing around with that stuff either; 23,000 of them died in one day because of it! And don't even think about trying to make Jesus your personal servant. They tried that, and God sent a bunch of poison snakes to deal with them. And stop complaining all the time, because that's what got them destroyed.

All these stories are like giant warning signs in our history book, telling us not to make the same clueless mistakes. We're in a similar spot as they were, just at a different time, and we can mess up just as easily. So don't be arrogant and think you're too good to fall. You could totally wipe out. Forget being self-confident; that's useless. Be God-confident.

Look, you're not going to face any temptation that's crazier than what other people have faced. Just remember that God's got your back. He'll never let you get pushed too far, and he'll always give you a way out.
So, my friends, when you see people trying to use God for their own selfish reasons, just run. Get away from them as fast as you can.

I'm talking to you like you're smart, so think about this: When we drink the cup of blessing, aren't we sharing in the life of Christ? And when we eat the bread, aren't we sharing in his body? Because there's one loaf of bread, we all become one body in Christ. He doesn't get broken up into a million pieces inside us; we become one with him. He lifts us up to his level. That's what happened with the Israelites too. When they ate the sacrifices, they were joining in with what God was doing at the altar.

See the difference? Sacrificing to idols is pointless because idols are nothing. Or even worse, they're demons! I don't want you getting mixed up in something that will bring you down. You can't be having a feast with Jesus one day and then hanging out with demons the next. Jesus won't stand for that. He wants all of you, or nothing at all. You think you can get away with anything less?

You could say, "I can do whatever I want." And yeah, because of God's grace, we don't have to stress about every little thing. But the goal isn't just to get by. We want to live awesome lives and help other people live awesome lives too.

So, use your common sense. You can eat anything you buy at the store; you don't have to ask if it was sacrificed to an idol. The whole earth belongs to God, and that includes the food at the store. If someone who isn't a believer invites you to dinner, go and have a good time. Eat whatever they serve you. It's rude to grill your host about where the food came from. But if they make a big deal about how the food was sacrificed to some idol, then you should probably pass. Even if you don't care, they do, and you don't want to send them mixed signals about who you worship.

But unless it's a situation like that, I'm not going to tiptoe around worrying about what other people think. I'm going to live freely because I know what God has said. If I'm thankful for my food, why should I worry about what someone else says?

So, whether you're eating or drinking or whatever, do it all to show how great God is. Don't be mean and use your freedom to trip up people who aren't as strong as you. I try to be considerate of everyone, and I hope you will too.

title: Don't Be That Guy at the Lord's Supper
paragraphs: §Worship Guidelines
Hey, major props to you all for sticking to the stuff I taught you. It's awesome that you remember. Just keep in mind that all real authority, the real power, comes from Jesus.

So, let's get the lineup straight. God is the head honcho, Jesus reports to God, and in a family, the husband is the team lead for the wife. It's all about respecting the chain of command. If a guy is praying or talking about God but acting like he's the boss instead of Jesus, he's totally disrespecting Christ. Same goes for a wife who publicly disses her husband's role—it makes them both look bad. It's just a terrible look, like a girl who has to shave her head. That's basically why we have these customs: guys take their hats off to show respect to Jesus, and women wear a covering to show they're part of the team structure. It's a visual way of saying, 'We're not fighting for control; we're all under God's ultimate authority.'

But don't get it twisted. This isn't about who's better. Guys and girls, you can't go it alone; you need each other. Sure, the first guy was a direct reflection of God's awesomeness, but let's be real, a woman's transformation is on another level. And yeah, the first woman came from a man, but every single guy since then has come from a woman! Since everything comes from God anyway, let's just drop the whole 'who's first' argument. It's a waste of time.
§Head Coverings

Doesn't it just make sense, though? There's something powerful about the symbolism: a woman with her awesome hair, looking like an angel, praying to God. And a guy, showing his respect with his head uncovered, submitting to God. I'm hoping you're not going to argue about this, because literally all the other churches are on the same page. I don't want you guys being the weird ones out.

Now, about this next thing... I'm not happy. I'm hearing that when you all get together, it's a total train wreck. Instead of bringing out the best in each other, it's bringing out the worst. First off, I'm getting reports that you're splitting into cliques, competing, and roasting each other. I don't want to believe it, but the evidence is there. I guess the only good thing is that this drama will eventually show who's for real and who's fake.

And then you bring that same divisive vibe to church! You come together for what's supposed to be the Lord's Supper, but instead, you turn it into a potluck where you just pig out. Some people get left out and go home hungry, while others get so ruined they have to be carried home. Seriously? Don't you have houses to eat and drink in? Why would you disrespect God's church like that and straight-up shame the people who don't have as much? I'm blown away that you'd stoop that low, and I'm not gonna stay quiet about it.

Let me remind you what the Lord's Supper is all about and why it's a big deal. I got these instructions straight from the Master himself. On the night he was betrayed, Jesus took some bread, thanked God for it, broke it, and said, 'This is my body, which is broken for you. Do this to remember me.'
After dinner, he did the same with the cup, saying, 'This cup is my blood, the new deal I'm making with you. Every time you drink this, remember me.'

Here's what you have to get: every time you eat this bread and drink this cup, you're basically re-enacting the Master's death with your actions and words. You're supposed to keep coming back to this meal until he returns. So don't let it become so routine that you stop thinking about what it means.

Anyone who eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Master without thinking, just going through the motions, is basically joining the crowd that mocked and spit on him when he died. Is that really the memory you want to be a part of? Check yourself before you wreck yourself. Come to this meal with some holy awe.

If you don't even think about the Master's broken body when you eat and drink, you're risking some serious trouble. That's why a lot of you are feeling weak and sick, and some have even died young. If we get our act together now, we won't have to get called out by God later. It's way better to get checked by the Master now than to face a fiery judgment down the road.

So, my friends, when you come together for the Lord's Table, be cool and respectful to each other. If you're so hungry you can't wait, just eat a sandwich at home first. Whatever you do, don't risk turning this sacred meal into a food fight or a family drama. It's a spiritual thing—a love feast.
As for the other questions you had, I'll deal with them in person when I visit next.

title: The Ultimate Superpower
paragraphs: §Spiritual Gifts

Alright, let's get real about how God's Spirit shows up in our lives. It's kinda complicated and people get it twisted, so I'm here to give you the lowdown. Remember back in the day when you didn't know God? You were just following the crowd, chasing after fake gods, not even knowing what you were doing. Total chaos, right? Well, things are different now. God wants you to use your brain and actually get what's going on. Like, you're smart enough to know that God's Spirit isn't gonna make you curse Jesus. And you can't truly say 'Jesus is the man!' unless the Holy Spirit is giving you that inside scoop.

God's giving out all sorts of awesome gifts, and they all come from his Spirit. He's got different jobs for everyone, but it's all powered by the same Spirit. God's power is showing up all over the place, and he's the one pulling the strings. Everyone gets a piece of the action, and it's all to show how amazing God is. The Spirit hands out a ton of different gifts to all kinds of people, and the variety is insane! You've got people who give amazing advice, others who just *get* things, some with rock-solid faith, and others who can heal people. Then there are the ones who do straight-up miracles, those who can speak God's truth, and even people who can tell the difference between good and evil spirits. Some can speak in different languages, and others can explain what they're saying. All these gifts come from the same place, the one and only Spirit of God. He's the one who decides who gets what and when. It's like he's building the ultimate squad.
§One Body, Many Parts

Think about your own body. It's got a bunch of different parts, right? Arms, legs, organs, whatever. But no matter how many parts you've got, you're still one body. It's the same with Christ. His Spirit brings us all together, and we ditch our old, separate lives. We used to do our own thing, but now we're part of something bigger, and He's the boss. That's what we signed up for when we got baptized. We're all part of his new-and-improved body, and we all drink from the same fountain – his Spirit. All those old labels we used to use, like where we're from or if we're popular or not, they don't matter anymore. We're all on the same team now.

This whole thing makes you a bigger deal, not a smaller one. A body isn't just one giant part. It's all the different parts working together. If your foot was like, 'I'm not as cool as the hand with all its bling, so I'm out,' would that even make sense? Or if your ear said, 'I'm not as pretty as the eye, so I don't belong here,' would you want to get rid of it? If your whole body was an eye, how would you hear anything? And if it was all ear, how would you smell? God put every single part of the body exactly where he wanted it.

But don't get a big head about it. You're only important because you're part of the team. A giant eye or a huge hand wouldn't be a body, it would be a total chaos. We're one body with lots of parts, all in the right place and the right size. No single part is the star of the show. Can you imagine your eye telling your hand, 'I don't need you'? Or your head telling your foot, 'You're fired'? It's actually the other way around. The parts that seem less important are actually the most essential. You can live without an eye, but you can't live without a stomach. When it comes to your own body, you don't care if a part is visible or not, or if it's 'high' or 'low.' You treat it with respect just the way it is. You probably even worry more about the 'lower' parts. I mean, if you had to choose, wouldn't you rather have a good stomach than a full head of hair?

The way God made our bodies is the perfect example of how we should live together as a church. Every part needs every other part. The parts we talk about and the parts we don't, the parts we see and the parts we don't. If one part is hurting, everyone feels it. And when one part is doing great, everyone celebrates. You guys are Christ's body – that's who you are! Don't ever forget it. Your 'part' only matters when you accept that you're part of the whole body. You know some of the roles God has set up in his church, his 'body': apostles, prophets, teachers, miracle workers, healers, helpers, organizers, and people who pray in tongues. But it's pretty obvious that Christ's church is a complete body, not just one giant, super-important part. It's not all apostles, or all prophets, or all miracle workers. And yet, some of you are still fighting over the 'important' jobs. But now, I'm going to show you a much better way.

title: Love is the Real MVP
paragraphs: §The Love Chapter

Look, you can talk a big game, sound super smart, or even have the voice of an angel, but if you don't have love, you're just making a bunch of annoying noise, like a squeaky hinge that needs some WD-40. Seriously, it's just noise.

And what if you're some kind of genius who can drop truth bombs, understand all of God's secret plans, and have faith so strong you could tell a mountain to take a hike and it would actually move? If you don't have love, you're still a nobody. A big zero. It's like having all the cheat codes but still losing the game.

You could give away everything you own, be a super generous person, and even be a martyr for your beliefs, but if you do it all without love, you've accomplished nothing. You're spiritually bankrupt. Without love, you're just faking it.
§What Love Looks Like

So what's the deal with love? It's like this: Love is patient and doesn't give up. It's all about caring for others more than yourself. It's not jealous or showing off. It doesn't get a big head or act all arrogant. It's not rude or pushy. It's not always demanding to be first. It doesn't have a short fuse and get angry over every little thing. It doesn't keep a list of all the times people have wronged you. It's not happy when people fail, but it celebrates the truth. It can handle anything. It always trusts God, always looks on the bright side, and never, ever quits.

Love is the one thing that's going to last forever. All the other stuff, like being able to give epic speeches, or speak in different languages, or having all the answers—that's all going to fade away. We only know a little bit of the big picture right now. But when the real deal, the complete picture, shows up, all our incomplete stuff will be a thing of the past.

Think about it like this: when you were a little kid, you talked and thought like a little kid. But when you grow up, you leave all that kid stuff behind. That's what it's like for us. Right now, we're like we're looking at a blurry picture, but one day we'll see everything clearly. We'll see God face-to-face and know him just like he knows us. How cool is that?
So, for now, we've got three main things to focus on: trusting God completely, hoping for the best, and loving like crazy. And the greatest of these, the real MVP, is love.

title: Superpowers in Church: Who Gets the Mic?
paragraphs: §Prophecy vs. Tongues

Alright, so, loving people is the absolute main thing. Like, your life is on the line—for real. And yeah, God gives out some awesome spiritual gifts, so you should totally be hype for those. But the one you should want most is being able to speak God's truth in a way everyone gets.

See, if you're praying in a secret prayer language, that's cool and all—God gets you, and it's like you two have your own private chat. But when you speak God's truth so everyone can understand, you're letting the whole squad in on it. That's how everyone grows and gets stronger together.

Praying in that private language is a good way to build yourself up, for sure. But speaking God's truth to the whole church? That's a total transformation for everyone. I want you all to have that tight connection with God in prayer, but don't just stop there. Go out and tell everyone his truth in plain English. It's way more important for everyone to get God's love and knowledge than for you to have some mysterious prayer time by yourself. Unless, of course, you've got someone who can translate for the whole crew.

Think about it, bros. If I show up and just start praying in a way only God understands, what good is that to you? If I don't drop some knowledge, or some truth, or some teaching, I'm no help at all. It's like a band where the instruments are all out of tune—you can't even tell what song they're playing. If the trumpet player just mashes random notes, who's gonna know it's time for battle?

So if you're just talking gibberish, what's the point? There are tons of languages in the world, and they all mean something to someone. But if I don't get your language, it's useless to me. Same goes for you guys. Since you're so pumped to be part of what God's doing, focus on what actually helps the whole church.

So, if you're gonna pray in your private language, don't be selfish with it. Pray that you can also explain it to everyone else. If I pray in tongues, my spirit is praying, but my brain is just chilling, not doing anything. That's a waste of brainpower! So here's the deal: do both. Pray with your spirit, but pray with your mind, too. Sing with your spirit, and sing with your mind. If you're blessing someone in your private language, and some new person shows up who has no clue what's going on, how are they supposed to say "Amen"? Your prayer might be awesome, but you totally ghosted that person.

I'm super thankful to God for the gift of praying in tongues. I do it as much as any of you. But when we're all together in church, I'd rather say five words that everyone understands and can learn from than ten thousand words that just sound like a bunch of noise.

Honestly, I'm getting tired of you guys thinking like little kids. When are you gonna grow up and use your heads? It's fine to be innocent when it comes to evil—just say no. But saying yes to God's stuff takes some serious brainpower. The Bible even says that God would preach to his people in weird languages, but they still wouldn't listen. So what's the point of speaking in tongues that no one gets? It doesn't help believers, and it just makes unbelievers think you're crazy. But when you speak plain truth, it hits believers right in the heart and doesn't weird out the unbelievers. If some outsiders walk in while you're all speaking in tongues, they're gonna think you've lost your minds and bounce. But if they walk in and you're all speaking God's truth, those words will hit them hard, and they'll realize God is really there with you.

So here's the game plan. When you all get together for church, come ready with something to share that will help everyone. Sing a song, teach a lesson, tell a story, lead a prayer, share some wisdom. If people are gonna pray in tongues, keep it to two or three people, and only if someone's there to translate. Otherwise, just keep it between you and God. And only two or three people should speak at a meeting, while everyone else listens and thinks about it. Take turns, don't let one person hog the mic. That way, everyone gets a chance to share something from God, and you all learn from each other. If you're gonna speak, you're responsible for how and when you do it. When we do church right, God doesn't make things chaotic; he makes them peaceful. This is how it should be in all the churches, no exceptions.

And ladies, don't be disrupting the service by talking when you should be listening. If you have questions, ask your husbands at home. The Bible gives us the rules on how to act in church. You don't have a license to just start talking whenever you want. And for everyone, guys and girls, do you really think you're the ones who get to decide what's right and wrong? Do you think you're the center of the universe?
If any of you think you have a message from God, then you better listen to what I'm writing. This is how the Boss wants it. If you're not gonna play by the rules, God can't use you. Sorry, not sorry.
So, to wrap it all up: when you're speaking God's truth, go all out. Don't tell people they can't pray in tongues if you don't understand them. And just be cool and respectful in everything you do.

title: The Ultimate Transformation
paragraphs: §The Resurrection

Alright guys, let's have a real talk about this whole Jesus thing one more time. This is the message I shared with you, the one you totally bought into, and the one that's saving you. That is, if you're actually sticking with it and not just treating it like some passing trend.

First things first, I told you what was super important: that Jesus, the real MVP, died for all our misfits, just like the old scrolls said he would. He was buried, and then on the third day, he came back to life, again, just like the scrolls predicted. He showed up to Peter, then to his whole squad, and later to a massive crowd of over 500 people at once! Most of them are still around to tell the tale, though some have since passed away. Then he hung out with James and the rest of the team he commissioned to rep him. And, believe it or not, he showed up to me last. It's kinda fitting, really. I don't even deserve to be in the inner circle, especially since I spent so much time trying to cancel the church.

But because God is so incredibly generous, here I am. And I'm not about to let his kindness go to waste. I've been grinding harder than anyone, but even then, it wasn't really me. It was God giving me the energy and the work to do. So, whether you heard it from me or the other guys, the message is the same: we told you God's truth, and you put your trust in it.

Now, here's a mind-bender for you. If you believe that Christ came back from the dead, how can some of you be saying there's no such thing as a resurrection? If there's no resurrection, then Christ is still dead. And let's be real, if Christ is still dead, then everything we've told you is fake news, and your faith is totally pointless. Not only that, but we'd be a bunch of liars, telling you that God flexed his power and raised Christ from the dead when he actually didn't.

If dead people can't be brought back, then Christ wasn't brought back. And if Christ wasn't brought back, you're all just stumbling around in the dark, as lost as ever. It's even worse for those who died believing in a resurrection, because they're just gone. If all we get out of following Jesus is a little inspiration for our short lives, we're a pretty sad bunch. But the truth is, Christ *did* have a miraculous transformation, the first of many who will be leaving their graves behind.

It all fits together perfectly. Death came into the world because of one man, and the resurrection from the dead came through another man. Everyone dies because of Adam, but everyone who is with Christ gets to live. But you gotta wait your turn. Christ is the first, then his followers will get their transformation when he returns. That's when he'll crush all his enemies and hand the kingdom over to God the Father. He won't stop until every enemy is defeated, and the final boss is death itself. Like the old song says, "He put them all under his feet." But obviously, he can't be under his own feet. When everything is under God's control, the Son will step aside, and God will be in charge of everything. A perfect ending!

And what's the deal with people getting baptized for their dead relatives? If there's no chance of a comeback, if God's power ends at the cemetery, why do people do things that suggest he's going to clear the whole place out one day?

And why do you think I'm always risking my life for this? I face death every single day. Do you think I'd do this if I wasn't 100% sure about the resurrection? Do you think I was just trying to be a hero when I fought those wild animals in Ephesus? No way! It's all about the resurrection. That's what fuels me. If there's no resurrection, then we might as well just say "YOLO," and eat, drink, and be merry, because that's all there is. But don't be fooled by those negativity. "Bad company ruins good character."

Get your heads straight and wake up to how holy life is. Stop playing around with the facts of the resurrection. You can't afford to be ignorant about God in times like these. Aren't you embarrassed that you've let this kind of talk go on for so long?

I know some skeptic is gonna ask, "How does this resurrection thing even work? What will our new bodies look like?" But that's a silly question. It's like gardening. You plant a dead-looking seed, and a whole plant grows. The seed and the plant look nothing alike. You'd never guess what a tomato plant looks like just by looking at the seed. What we bury and what grows are totally different. Our dead bodies and our resurrection bodies will be a dramatic upgrade.

And the variety of bodies is insane! Just like there are different kinds of seeds, there are different kinds of bodies—people, animals, birds, fish. You can get a hint of the different kinds of resurrection glory by looking at the sky—the sun, moon, and stars all have their own brightness. And we're just looking at the "seeds" now. Who can even imagine what the "plants" will be like!

This whole seed thing is just a small picture, but maybe it helps you understand the mystery of the resurrection body. The body we bury is weak and unimpressive, but when it's raised, it's glorious and powerful. It goes from a natural body to a supernatural one. Same body, but what a transformation from mortal to immortal!

It's like this: the first Adam was a living being, but the last Adam (that's Jesus) is a life-giving Spirit. We start with a physical life, made from the earth, but we end with a spiritual life, from heaven. We all started out earthy, like Adam 1.0, but now we can be heavenly, like Adam 2.0. So let's embrace our heavenly destiny.
I gotta stress this, friends: our current bodies just aren't built for God's kingdom. They're designed to die, so how could they naturally end up in a kingdom of life?

But let me tell you a secret, a mystery I'll probably never fully get. We're not all going to die, but we're all going to be changed. In the blink of an eye, at the sound of the last trumpet, it'll all be over. The dead will be raised with brand-new bodies that will never die again. And in that same moment, we who are still alive will get our epic upgrade. This has to happen. The perishable has to be replaced by the imperishable, the mortal by the immortal. Then the old saying will come true:
Death is totally owned by Life!
Who gets the last word now, Death?
Who's afraid of you anymore?
Sin is what made death so scary, and the law is what gave sin its power. But in one single move, Jesus took out all three—sin, guilt, and death. It's a gift from our master, Jesus Christ. Thank God!

So with all this going for us, my dear friends, stand your ground. Don't back down. Throw yourselves into the Master's work, because you can be sure that nothing you do for him is ever a waste of time or effort.

title: Paul's Wrap-Up & Final Instructions
paragraphs: §The Collection and Goodbyes

Alright guys, last chapter. Let's talk about the fundraiser for the Christians who are having a tough time. I'm giving you the same game plan I gave the churches in Galatia. Every Sunday, each of you should set aside some cash, whatever you can afford. Be generous. That way, when I show up, it's all ready to go and I don't have to do some big fundraising push. Once I'm there, you can pick a few trusted people, I'll write them some recommendation letters, and they can be the crew that delivers your gift to Jerusalem. If it seems like a good idea for me to go too, I'll totally travel with them.

I'm planning to swing by and visit you after I pass through northern Greece. I'm not staying there long, but I'm hoping to have a good, long visit with you guys—maybe even crash for the winter. Then you can give me a solid send-off for my next destination. I don't want to just make a quick cameo; I want a real, chill visit. If God's cool with it, it'll happen. For now, I'm staying here in Ephesus. A massive door of opportunity just opened up for some major work, but, not gonna lie, the opposition is leveling up too.

If my boy Timothy shows up, make sure you take good care of him. He's grinding for the Lord just as hard as I am, so make him feel at home. Don't let anyone roast him or look down on him. When he's ready to leave, send him off with your blessing. I'm expecting him and any friends he brings along.
About our buddy Apollos, I've been trying to get him to visit you, but he's not feeling the timing right now. He basically ghosted the idea for now, but he promises there will be a right time.
§Final Shout-Outs
Okay, final pep talk. Stay woke, hold on tight to what you believe, and give it everything you've got. Be absolute units, and make sure love is the main quest in everything you do.

And hey, can you do me a favor? Give a major shout-out to the family of Stephanas. You know they were some of the first to join the squad in Greece, and they've been total servants to other Christians ever since. You gotta respect and look up to people like that, the real ones who show us how it's done.

I'm so stoked to have Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus here with me. They're awesome and totally make up for you guys not being here. They've been a huge encouragement and keep me in the loop with you all. You should be proud to have people like them in your crew.

The churches over here in western Asia send their greetings. Aquila and Priscilla, and the church that meets in their house, all say what's up. All the friends here say hi. Give each other some holy hugs.
And this part is from me, Paul—in my own handwriting so you know it's real!—I'm sending you my best.
If anyone doesn't have love for the Lord, kick 'em out. Make room for the Master!
May our Lord Jesus be super generous with you.
And I love all of you in Jesus, for real.
